dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: Aug 17-18: SpaceX's Biggest Shareholders Revealed in 13F Wave — SPCX Whipsaws Between +4.45% and -3.2%
heroSubtitle: 8,870 days since SpaceX founding — Mid-August Form 13F filings revealed SpaceX's largest institutional shareholders for the first time since its June IPO: Alphabet (~551M shares, ~$94B), Fidelity, Gigafund, Saudi Arabia's PIF, and Nvidia (~$21B via its xAI stake), plus first-time positions from AMD and Harvard Management, sending SPCX up 4.45% to $146.23 on Aug 17. Shares gave back roughly 3% on Aug 18 amid a broader growth-stock selloff, new US tariffs, and profit-taking ahead of an ~319M-share unlock due Aug 20 — even after SpaceX signed a new Transporter rideshare launch contract for Vietnamese operator VinSpace's first satellites. That volatility followed an Aug 15 launch-cadence record: two Falcon 9 missions (Globalstar 2-R and the classified USSF-366) lifted off just 38.5 minutes apart from opposite coasts, SpaceX's 96th Falcon-family launch of 2026 and the 650th cumulative booster landing in company history. SpaceX also closed its $60B all-stock acquisition of Cursor-maker Anysphere on Aug 14, and a filing showed Musk's 48.4% economic stake worth over $900B. On the Starship side, Booster 21 and Ship 41 continue static-fire preparations at Starbase toward IFT-14, tentatively targeting late August pending FAA approval.
